title: A Whale Closed Its Mouth Around a Lobster Diver. Then It Spat Him Out
description:
Case 004, the full case file. On Friday 11 June 2021, off Herring Cove at the tip of Cape Cod, lobster diver Michael Packard, 56, was about 45 feet down when he felt a huge shove and everything went black. He thought it was a great white shark. There were no teeth. He was inside the mouth of a humpback whale, still breathing from his tank, sure he was about to die. Thirty to forty seconds later the whale surfaced, shook its head and threw him out. This is the whole case: the morning on the boat, the crewman who follows the bubbles, the regulator in the dark, the second witness who saw him come out feet first, the run for the Provincetown pier, the hospital that found bruises and no broken bones, the newspaper reporter who says he was asked to debunk it and made a documentary instead, and the whale scientists who explain why it was an accident and why a humpback could never have swallowed him. Rook, Survra's sceptical crow detective, did not believe it either.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. Rook, the boat, the rooms and the people's appearance are dramatised; the facts are from the sources below.

source_notes: Re-checked on 13 Nov 2026 against the pages listed in sources. CCT = Doug Fraser's Cape Cod Times report of 11 June 2021, read in the cob-net.org reprint because capecodtimes.com could not be opened. Who, when, where: Michael Packard, 56, of Wellfleet (AP via WBUR, CCT); Friday 11 June 2021, off Provincetown; crewman Josiah Mayo (CCT, NPR; CNN calls him the captain). CCT puts the boat off Herring Cove Beach, the Boston Globe off Race Point; the script and map follow CCT. The job: divers pluck lobsters off the sandy bottom and the crewman follows the diver's bubbles (CCT). The dive: 'a little before 8 a.m.', water 60 degrees, visibility about 20 feet (CCT). CCT calls it his second dive, Josiah Mayo (WGBH) and the Globe his third, so the script only says he 'goes in again'. Depth: 'about 45 feet deep' (AP, CNN) or 'about 10 feet from the bottom' (CCT); the script says 'in forty-five feet of water' and 'nearly at the bottom'. Inside: a 'huge shove' and 'completely black' (CCT; AP has 'huge bump' and 'dark'); he thought of a great white, felt no teeth and 'no great pain' (CCT, CNN); he could sense he was moving and feel the mouth muscles squeezing (CCT); he feared being swallowed or running out of air (NBC, CNN). Regulator: the first-day reports (AP, NPR, Live Science) only say he kept breathing through it; the Globe, NBC and his own later account say it came out and he recovered it, so the script says 'by his later account'. He thought of his wife and his two boys (CCT, CNN; the older son's age differs between sources, so no ages are given). 30 to 40 seconds by his own estimate (CCT, NPR; AP says about 30). He struggled, the whale shook its head, he saw light and was thrown clear (CCT, CNN). Witnesses: Josiah Mayo saw 'a huge eruption of water' and first thought of a shark attack (WGBH; CCT); charter captain Joe Francis said he saw him 'come flying out of the water, feet first with his flippers on' (NPR, from WBZ-TV). Rescue: Mayo picked him up, called shore by radio and went in to the Provincetown pier; a Provincetown Fire Department ambulance took him to Cape Cod Hospital (CCT; the Globe says Mayo called 911). Injuries: his sister first reported a broken leg (AP); he was released that afternoon with soft tissue damage and no broken bones (CCT, NPR). A dislocated knee (NBC, Smithsonian) and torn ligaments (Globe) are also reported and are not asserted. No source read describes a limp, so the script and the animation no longer show one. The sceptic: Boston Globe reporter David Abel says his editor told him to debunk the story; he obtained the 911 tape and interviewed Packard, his family and the witnesses, and his documentary 'In the Whale' premiered in June 2023 (BU Today, WGBH). The script names neither man and attributes no words to the editor; the on-screen card says THE ASSIGNMENT: DEBUNK IT. The science: an accident during lunge feeding on sand lance (Jooke Robbins and Charles 'Stormy' Mayo, Center for Coastal Studies: CCT, AP, CNN); an open mouth blocks the whale's forward vision (Robbins, CCT); the throat is too small for a person (Robbins, CCT and CNN; Kerr, NPR; no measurement is given on screen). Stormy Mayo is Josiah Mayo's father (CCT) and made the meal-and-fly comparison (CNN), which the script paraphrases without quotation marks. Before and after: he survived a 2001 plane crash in Costa Rica in which three of the eight aboard died (CCT, Smithsonian, AP 2001; accounts differ on how long the rescue took, so the script gives no duration and no numbers); on Jimmy Kimmel Live that week he apologised to the whale for getting in its way (NBC Boston); he was back lobster diving within about three weeks (Newsweek, WGBH 2023). Dramatised, not reported: the look of the boat, pier, ambulance bay, hospital room, newsroom and whale lab; everyone's appearance and clothes; the lobster under the ledge; the exact way the whale approached and the breach beside the boat (sources say it surfaced and threw him out); the family photograph (three plain silhouettes); the X-ray card (a graphic for 'no broken bones', not a real film); the fluke at dusk; and everything Rook does. No dialogue is attributed to anyone.

quality_gate.method: 3D contact sheet reviewed in four rounds (the last at full frame size for eight key shots), composited stills (captions, HUD, overlays, inserts) in one, and a three-frames-per-shot strip from a full-length low-resolution rehearsal (216x384, 4 samples), which passed the automated gate locally: 39 shots, mean 1.11 s, longest 1.56 s, loudness -15.0 LUFS, voice 11.9 dB over the bed, host in 17/39 shots (44%), closest match to an earlier episode 0.78; caption pairs were measured against the frame width and the script reworded where a pair overflowed; the regulator's colour was changed after the rehearsal and not re-rendered; audio was measured, not listened to; the full-resolution render and final gate run in the cloud
